title: EXP-064 - Hello World Part 4 Section 6a: Create the FX_HelloWorld Theme with an FX_BlueButton Button Class
objective: Follow hello-world-pt4.md Section 6 steps 1-8 (05:51-07:29), adapted to FX_ names, in the Web Designer. Through the Designer Edit Themes command, create a new theme named FX_HelloWorld and open it for editing. In its Form Component tree, select Button, enter FX_BlueButton as the Class Name and add it. Select Button > FX_BlueButton and its Normal state, set Background Color to the tutorial literal #FF5CC6C7 exactly as typed (eight hexadecimal digits; never reinterpret it), and set Foreground Color through its picker to Solid with the default White. Save the theme once, close the theme editor once, reopen FX_HelloWorld for editing once, and verify that the FX_BlueButton class and both colors persisted. This experiment changes no User Preference, Form, component or other theme; selecting the theme in User Preferences and applying the class to the Import button are a later experiment. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md and docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt4.md Section 6 (05:51-07:29) before browser interaction.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-064-hello-world-part-4-section-6a-theme-and-button-class.md and evidence/EXP-064/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.
Use the existing authenticated session without reauthentication, refresh, restart or configuration change. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection.

Identify the Web Designer tab, any Form open in it and its dirty state. Locate the Edit Themes command through the visible Designer menus or toolbar and record its exact label and route. Leave any open Designer Form untouched.
Open Edit Themes and record the existing theme list and the available controls. If FX_HelloWorld already exists, stop before any change and report it.

Create the FX_HelloWorld theme once through the supported native create control of the theme dialog. If creation requires choosing a base theme, choose the default offered by the dialog and record it; the base theme itself stays unchanged.
Open FX_HelloWorld for editing once. In the Form Component tree select Button, type FX_BlueButton into Class Name and add it once; verify the tree shows Button > FX_BlueButton.

Select Button > FX_BlueButton, then the Normal state. Set Background Color to #FF5CC6C7 as an exact literal and record the readback verbatim. Open the Foreground Color picker, choose Solid, keep the default White, confirm, and record the readback verbatim.
Save the theme exactly once through the native control and record the native response verbatim.

Close the theme editor once, reopen FX_HelloWorld for editing once, and verify that Button > FX_BlueButton exists with the recorded Normal Background and Foreground values. Then close the theme dialogs, ending with no theme dialog open.
Verify that the theme list contains the original themes plus FX_HelloWorld only.
Capture screenshots when Edit Themes is first opened, before the theme is created, after creation, after the class is added, with each color set, after Save and after the reopen.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.

acceptance_checks.description: Sources reviewed; session usable without challenge; the Web Designer tab identified with any open Form and its dirty state recorded; the exact Edit Themes label and route recorded; the original theme list recorded with no FX_HelloWorld present. Evidence: tab list, Edit Themes route and theme-list screenshots.

The FX_HelloWorld theme was created once through the native create control (any base theme recorded and left unchanged) and opened for editing. Evidence: before/after screenshots and the create-control audit.
In the Form Component tree, FX_BlueButton was added once under Button and the tree shows Button > FX_BlueButton. Evidence: screenshot of the tree.

For Button > FX_BlueButton > Normal: Background Color was entered as #FF5CC6C7 and its readback recorded verbatim; Foreground Color was set through the picker to Solid White and its readback recorded verbatim. Evidence: screenshots with each value visible.
Exactly one theme Save; the native response recorded verbatim; no unsaved-change indication remains. Evidence: pre/post-Save screenshots and the Save count.

The theme editor was closed once and FX_HelloWorld reopened for editing once; Button > FX_BlueButton exists with the same Normal Background and Foreground readbacks. Evidence: reopen route and screenshots.

No other change: the theme list is the original list plus FX_HelloWorld; no User Preference, Designer Form or component change; no theme dialog left open. Evidence: final theme-list screenshot and the audit.

The final EXP-064 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-7, the complete action audit with exact counts (one theme create, one class add, two color changes, one theme Save, one close/reopen, zero other theme edits, zero preference changes, zero Form changes), the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.
